chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Hafs ibn Aasim, from Sayf al-Tammari, from Abu al-Murhaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The dust [of defeat/humiliation] is upon the one who raises it. Destroyed are the al-Mahadhir (the hasty ones). I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and who are the al-Mahadhir?' He said, 'The hasty ones. Indeed, they will not want anyone except the one who duels with them.' Then he said, 'O Abu al-Murhaf, indeed if they want to afflict you with a calamity, Allah, Exalted and Majestic, will present them with a distraction.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) tapped the ground with his finger and said, 'O Abu al-Murhaf!' I said, 'Here I am (at your service)!' He said, 'Do you see a people who have restricted themselves for the sake of Allah, Exalted is His mention, that Allah will not make a way out for them? Yes, by Allah, Allah will surely make a way out for them.'

key_terms.الْمَحَاضِيرُ: The hasty ones; those who rush to meet their enemies or opponents.
key_terms.حَبَسُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: To restrict or dedicate oneself (to God's service).
key_terms.فَرَجاً: A way out, relief, or deliverance from distress.

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Mahadhir' and what is the promise for those who restrict themselves to Allah?
